deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 146-147): Grothendieck proves a continuity theorem. If A_i → A in L^1, the trace class (or the L^1 of an algebra 𝔄), then the eigenvalue sequences Â_i → Â in Σ_p, i.e. in ℓ^p modulo ordering. Here r_ν(A) = |λ_ν(A)| are the moduli of the eigenvalues, s_ν = r_ν(|A|) are the singular values, and S_p(A) = Σ r_ν^p.

The key lemma: for every ε > 0 there exist ρ > 0 and i_0 such that Σ_{r_ν(A_i) ≤ ρ} r_ν(A_i)^p ≤ ε for all i ≥ i_0. In other words, the small eigenvalues carry uniformly small p-mass.

Step 1, the reduction (previous page):
- Take the convex function ω(t), equal to e^{pt} for t ≤ log ρ and to its tangent line beyond.
- Weyl's majorization inequality gives Σ ω(log |λ_ν|) ≤ Σ ω(log s_ν).
- Since |A_i| → |A| in L^1, this reduces the lemma to the case A_i ≥ 0. There one must show that Σ_{r ≤ ρ} r^p + ρ^p Σ_{r ≥ ρ} log(e (r/ρ)^p) is uniformly small.
- The proof splits this into (a), the tail term, and (b), the small-eigenvalue term.

Step 2, part (a), started on the previous page and finished here:
- Let n(r) = #{ν : r_ν ≥ r}. A Stieltjes integration by parts gives ρ^p Σ_{r_ν ≥ ρ} log(e (r_ν/ρ)^p) = ρ^p n(ρ) + p ρ^p ∫_ρ^∞ n(r)/r dr.
- The first term → 0 because Σ r_ν^p < ∞.
- On this page he argues that ∫ n(r)/r^{1+p} dr < ∞ implies 'a fortiori' ∫_0^∞ n(r)/r dr < ∞. Hence p ρ^α ∫_ρ^∞ n/r ≤ p ρ^α ∫_0^∞ n/r → 0.

Crossed-out block: an abandoned attempt to handle the general case by telescoping. If Σ ||A_{i+1} − A_i||_p < ∞ and Σ S_p(A_{i+1} − A_i) < ∞, then A = Σ (A_{i+1} − A_i), so A ≤ Σ |A_{i+1} − A_i|.

Step 3, part (b): for A_i ≥ 0,
- Σ_{r_ν(A_i) ≤ ρ} r_ν^p = S_p(A_i) − Σ_{r_ν(A_i) > ρ} r_ν^p.
- This tends to S_p(A) − Σ_{r_ν > ρ} r_ν^p = Σ_{r_ν ≤ ρ} r_ν^p, using convergence of S_p and of the finitely many large eigenvalues.
- So choose ρ with Σ_{r_ν ≤ ρ} r_ν^p < ε, then i large.

The next page moves on to Fredholm theory: the resolvent R(u) = det(1+u)/(1+u), the coefficients P_n(u), and bounds by e^{||u||_1}. This is material for 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956) and the eigenvalue-distribution results in Produits tensoriels topologiques, Ch. II.
errors: The 'a fortiori' step is wrong as written. With n(r) = #{r_ν ≥ r} (the convention forced by the previous page's integration by parts), n(r) → ∞ as r → 0 whenever there are infinitely many nonzero eigenvalues. Then ∫_0^∞ n(r)/r dr = +∞, and the bound by ρ^α ∫_0^∞ n/r is vacuous.
With the other convention (n counting the zeros 1/r_ν, Nevanlinna style), ∫ n/r^{1+p} < ∞ does not imply ∫ n/r < ∞ either, since the implication fails at infinity.
The correct condition is Σ r_ν^p = p ∫ n(r) r^{p−1} dr < ∞.

The conclusion ρ^p ∫_ρ^∞ n(r)/r dr → 0 is nevertheless true, and the gap is easy to repair. First route: it equals Σ_{r_ν ≥ ρ} ρ^p log(r_ν/ρ), each term is ≤ r_ν^p/(pe) and → 0, so dominated convergence applies. Second route: split the integral at a fixed σ.
'ρ^α' is evidently a slip for ρ^p.

Part (b) needs S_p(A_i) → S_p(A) for positive A_i → A in L^1. For p ≥ 1 this follows, since ||·||_p ≤ ||·||_1 and S_p(A) = ||A||_p^p. For p < 1, tr A^p is not continuous in trace norm, so the argument tacitly assumes p ≥ 1.
Part (b) also needs ρ chosen not to be an eigenvalue of A, so that the large eigenvalues converge. This is left implicit.

ideas.what: Using Weyl's majorization Σ ω(log|λ_ν|) ≤ Σ ω(log s_ν), with a convex ω that is exponential then linear, to reduce eigenvalue estimates to the positive case.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's inequality / log-majorization of eigenvalues by singular values
ideas.where_published: Probably used in Produits tensoriels topologiques Ch. II and/or La théorie de Fredholm (1956)

ideas.what: Continuity of the eigenvalue sequence: A_i → A in trace class implies eigenvalue sequences converge in ℓ^p (Σ_p), via uniform smallness of the small-eigenvalue tail.
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of spectra in Schatten classes / Lidskii–Markus type eigenvalue perturbation

ideas.what: Counting-function / Stieltjes integration-by-parts estimate of tail sums.
ideas.modern_name: Counting function n(r) of eigenvalues (entire-function style)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine lemma, with a fixable slip, inside a proof of continuity of eigenvalue sequences in trace class. The result and its Weyl-inequality method are standard (Gohberg–Krein, Markus) and close to Grothendieck's own Fredholm-theory work. It is mildly interesting as an early 1953 use of Weyl majorization, but nothing appears to be absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ρ^α' in line 2 is in the manuscript, but is likely meant as ρ^p.
In the crossed-out block the last formula reads 'A ≤ Σ |A_{i+1} − A_i|' (an inequality), not 'A ∈ ...'.
In part (b), '→' was first written followed by a crossed-out '≤'. The relation subscript under the sums was also corrected (> vs ≤) in the manuscript.
